# Doctor checks

`opencode-unity doctor` runs the checks below. Each one has a stable id: `doctor --explain <id>` prints
the same rationale at the terminal, and `doctor --json` reports every id with its outcome.

Severity is what a check reports when it finds something. A check that finds nothing reports `ok`, and a
check whose subject is absent reports `skipped` with the reason. Before `opencode-unity setup` has run on
a machine there is no configuration to be wrong, so a check that would report `ERROR` about this
product's own configuration reports `WARN` instead and says so; `--strict` still fails on it.

Exit codes: `0` with no errors, `5` with at least one error, or with at least one warning under
`--strict`.

Checks in this build: 47.

## Platform support

| Check | Reports | What it detects, and why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `platform.tier` | ERROR / INFO | A tier says how much of this product has been run on this kind of machine, which decides what every other finding is worth. |
| `platform.accelerator-backend` | WARN / INFO | The guard decides from free video memory. Without an accelerator probe it cannot read any, so it fails closed instead of protecting anything. |
| `platform.probe-missing` | ERROR / WARN | A capability with no probe behind it is not a passing check, it is an unasked question, and the guard has to treat it as one. |
| `platform.virtualized-host` | ERROR | Inside WSL or a container every probe answers, and answers about the wrong machine: the Unity Editor and the display driver live on the host. |
| `platform.unified-memory-cap` | INFO | On Apple silicon the model and the rest of the system share one memory pool, so a video-memory headroom number measured on a discrete card does not transfer. |
| `platform.linux-ollama-journal` | WARN | On Linux the Ollama server log is the systemd journal. Without access to it the truncation history cannot be read at all. |
| `node.global-prefix-writable` | WARN | A global install run with sudo leaves root-owned files that a later upgrade or uninstall cannot remove without sudo again. |

### `platform.tier` — Support tier for this machine

- Reports: ERROR / INFO
- Fix: Run the refused commands on a supported machine, or pass --experimental to accept an experimental row.
- Source: amendment 33.4 and src/core/tiers.json

### `platform.accelerator-backend` — Accelerator backend

- Reports: WARN / INFO
- Fix: Install the vendor tool the backend needs, or accept that the guard blocks rather than measures on this machine.
- Source: amendment 33.5, 33.6 and spec 7.2

### `platform.probe-missing` — Guard probes available here

- Reports: ERROR / WARN
- Fix: Run on a platform whose probes ship in this version, or expect blocked verdicts instead of measured ones.
- Source: amendment 33.6 result algebra

### `platform.virtualized-host` — Virtualized host

- Reports: ERROR
- Fix: Run opencode-unity on the host instead.
- Source: amendment CP-D11 and src/core/tiers.json
- Keeps its severity even before this product is set up on the machine.

### `platform.unified-memory-cap` — Unified memory on macOS

- Reports: INFO
- Fix: Treat the guard headroom values as uncalibrated here and watch memory pressure yourself.
- Source: amendment 33.5 and the preset gating of 33.4

### `platform.linux-ollama-journal` — Ollama journal readable

- Reports: WARN
- Fix: Add your user to the systemd-journal group, or pass --logs <path>.
- Source: amendment 33.8 and R22

### `node.global-prefix-writable` — Global npm prefix writable

- Reports: WARN
- Fix: Point npm at a prefix you own (npm config set prefix), or use a Node version manager, instead of installing globally with sudo.
- Source: amendment R21

## Installation

| Check | Reports | What it detects, and why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `setup.not-installed` | INFO | Without a config.json the report describes the machine rather than an installation, and findings that would be errors about a setup are reported one level lower. |
| `config.valid` | ERROR / WARN | An unreadable or unknown key in config.json stops every command that needs the runtime profile, which is all of them except this one. |
| `config.preset` | ERROR / WARN | The preset decides the model tag, the context size and the guard thresholds, so a preset that does not resolve leaves nothing else to check. |
| `setup.profile-rendered` | WARN | The launcher starts OpenCode against the profile rendered for the installed CLI version; an older one is not what this version expects. |

### `setup.not-installed` — opencode-unity installed here

- Reports: INFO
- Fix: Run opencode-unity setup to install the profile and the model.
- Source: spec 6.1 and 14.1

### `config.valid` — config.json parses and validates

- Reports: ERROR / WARN
- Fix: Fix the reported key, or move config.json aside and run opencode-unity setup again.
- Source: spec 6.2 and schema/config.schema.json

### `config.preset` — Preset usable on this machine

- Reports: ERROR / WARN
- Fix: Choose a shipped preset with opencode-unity setup --preset <id>, or pass --experimental to accept an experimental one.
- Source: spec 10.1 and amendment 33.4 preset gating

### `setup.profile-rendered` — Clean-room profile rendered for this version

- Reports: WARN
- Fix: Run opencode-unity upgrade to render the profile for this version.
- Source: spec 6.1 and 14.3

## Ollama

| Check | Reports | What it detects, and why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `ollama.reachable` | ERROR | Every model call goes to this endpoint; when it does not answer, nothing about the model, its context size or its parameters can be checked. |
| `ollama.version` | WARN | The log parser, the truncation limits and the unload behaviour were read from one Ollama version; an older one behaves differently in ways this report would not notice. |
| `ollama.loopback` | WARN | A remote endpoint means the GPU guard measures this machine and the model runs on another, so the guard protects nothing and prompts leave the machine. |

### `ollama.reachable` — Ollama answers

- Reports: ERROR
- Fix: Start Ollama, or point ollama.baseUrl in config.json at the server you use.
- Source: spec 4.5 and 6.2

### `ollama.version` — Ollama version tested

- Reports: WARN
- Fix: Update Ollama to the tested version, or accept that findings from the server log may be wrong.
- Source: compat.json and spec 3.2

### `ollama.loopback` — Ollama endpoint is loopback

- Reports: WARN
- Fix: Point ollama.baseUrl at a loopback address, or set guard.remote deliberately and accept that the guard cannot see that machine.
- Source: spec P11 and 7.3

## Model

| Check | Reports | What it detects, and why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `model.installed` | ERROR | The launcher pins one model tag; when Ollama does not have it, the first request fails with a provider error rather than a useful message. |
| `model.system-ignored` | WARN | A SYSTEM line baked into the model is dropped as soon as the client sends its own system message, so it reads like configuration that is doing nothing. |
| `model.num-ctx` | WARN | Without num_ctx in the model parameters the server falls back to its own default, which is usually far smaller than the profile assumes, and prompts are cut. |
| `model.renderer` | WARN | A qwen3-coder model whose renderer or parser is something else emits tool calls as text, which the agent then cannot execute. |

### `model.installed` — Configured model installed

- Reports: ERROR
- Fix: Run opencode-unity setup to create the model tag from the preset.
- Source: spec 10.3 and 14.1

### `model.system-ignored` — Modelfile SYSTEM prompt

- Reports: WARN
- Fix: Recreate the model tag from the shipped Modelfile, which has no SYSTEM line.
- Source: spec 10.3 and evidence E4

### `model.num-ctx` — Model context size pinned

- Reports: WARN
- Fix: Recreate the model tag from the preset so the Modelfile sets num_ctx.
- Source: spec 10.3 and evidence E1

### `model.renderer` — Renderer and parser match the model family

- Reports: WARN
- Fix: Recreate the model tag from the preset, which sets the renderer and the parser.
- Source: spec 10.1 and 10.3

## OpenCode

| Check | Reports | What it detects, and why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `opencode.version` | WARN | The permission rules, the tool list and the plugin hooks were read from one OpenCode version; another one can move any of them without an error. |
| `opencode.no-limit` | ERROR | A model entry without a limit leaves OpenCode with no context size to plan against, so it never compacts and the server truncates the prompt instead. |
| `opencode.limit-exceeds-numctx` | ERROR | When the declared context is larger than the model actually holds, the prompt is cut on the server and the agent loses the part it needed most. |
| `opencode.temperature-capability` | ERROR | Without the capability the sampling settings are dropped and the request runs at the provider defaults, which is the loosest setting there is. |
| `opencode.config-unreadable` | WARN | OpenCode skips a configuration file it cannot parse, so a file meant to deny something silently denies nothing. |

### `opencode.version` — OpenCode version tested

- Reports: WARN
- Fix: Install the tested OpenCode version, or run opencode-unity doctor --selftest for the version you have.
- Source: compat.json and spec D21

### `opencode.no-limit` — Model entries declare a limit

- Reports: ERROR
- Fix: Add "limit": { "context": <num_ctx>, "output": <max tokens> } to the model entry.
- Source: spec 8.3 and evidence E7

### `opencode.limit-exceeds-numctx` — limit.context fits the model context

- Reports: ERROR
- Fix: Lower limit.context to the model num_ctx, or recreate the model tag with a larger num_ctx.
- Source: spec 8.8 and evidence E1

### `opencode.temperature-capability` — Model entries declare the temperature capability

- Reports: ERROR
- Fix: Add "temperature": true to the model entry.
- Source: spec 8.3 and evidence E3

### `opencode.config-unreadable` — OpenCode config files parse

- Reports: WARN
- Fix: Fix the reported file, or move it aside.
- Source: spec 8.2

## Instruction files

| Check | Reports | What it detects, and why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `instructions.injected` | WARN | OpenCode prepends the project instruction files it finds above the working directory to every request, whether or not they are relevant to the task. |
| `instructions.nested` | WARN | A nested instruction file is attached the moment the agent reads any file beneath it, so it lands in the middle of a session with no way to decline it. |
| `unity.facts-cap` | ERROR | The facts file is part of the fixed prefix of every request, so a file over the cap takes context away from the task on every single turn. |

### `instructions.injected` — Instruction files added to every request

- Reports: WARN
- Fix: Shorten the file, or launch with --no-project-config so the session does not read project instruction files.
- Source: OpenCode session/instruction.ts and evidence E5

### `instructions.nested` — Nested instruction files under Assets and Packages

- Reports: WARN
- Fix: Move the guidance into the project instruction file, or delete the nested copies.
- Source: OpenCode session/instruction.ts nested attachment

### `unity.facts-cap` — Project facts within the cap

- Reports: ERROR
- Fix: Run opencode-unity init --refresh to rewrite the facts, or shorten your edits to it.
- Source: spec 9.6

## Tools and MCP

| Check | Reports | What it detects, and why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `tools.mcp-schema` | ERROR | Enabled MCP servers add their whole tool schema to every request, and nothing in the configuration denies those tools to the local model. |
| `mcp.duplicate-server` | ERROR | Two entries that differ only in case, or that point at the same URL, make the same tools appear twice and double what every request pays for them. |
| `mcp.hub-loopback` | WARN | A non-loopback hub means editor commands and their arguments leave the machine, and the instance the hub answers for is not necessarily the project open here. |

### `tools.mcp-schema` — MCP tool schemas reaching a local model

- Reports: ERROR
- Fix: Deny the server's tools for this agent, or disable the server, and keep only the tools the agent is meant to call.
- Source: spec 8.5 and 11.2

### `mcp.duplicate-server` — Duplicate MCP server entries

- Reports: ERROR
- Fix: Keep one entry per server and remove the duplicates.
- Source: spec 5.4

### `mcp.hub-loopback` — MCP hub address is loopback

- Reports: WARN
- Fix: Point the MCP server url at a loopback address.
- Source: spec 11.4 and P11

## Prompt budget

| Check | Reports | What it detects, and why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `budget.fixed-prefix` | ERROR / WARN | Tool schemas and project facts are sent before the task is; what they take is taken from every turn of the conversation, not once. |
| `budget.truncation-limit` | ERROR | Past the context size the server keeps the first few tokens and the tail and drops the middle, which is where the task and the file usually are. |

### `budget.fixed-prefix` — Fixed prefix against the budget

- Reports: ERROR / WARN
- Fix: Shorten the facts file, or reduce the tools the agent sees, until the prefix is back under the target.
- Source: spec 8.8

### `budget.truncation-limit` — Prompt budget below the server truncation limit

- Reports: ERROR
- Fix: Lower limit.context, or recreate the model tag with a larger num_ctx.
- Source: spec 8.8 and evidence E1

## Ollama server log

| Check | Reports | What it detects, and why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `logs.truncation` | ERROR / WARN | A truncated prompt keeps the first few tokens and the tail, so the agent silently loses the middle of what it was told and answers about the rest. |
| `logs.sampling-default` | WARN | A sampler at temperature one and top_p one means the request carried no sampling settings, which for a coding model is the least reliable setting available. |

### `logs.truncation` — Prompts the server truncated

- Reports: ERROR / WARN
- Fix: Lower limit.context to the model num_ctx, or recreate the model tag with a larger num_ctx.
- Source: Ollama llm/llama_server.go and evidence E1

### `logs.sampling-default` — Requests that ran at the sampler defaults

- Reports: WARN
- Fix: Add "temperature": true to the model entry so OpenCode sends the sampling settings.
- Source: evidence E3

## GPU

| Check | Reports | What it detects, and why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `vram.headroom` | ERROR / WARN | The preset states what the model needs; the guard refuses a load that would leave the rest of the machine below its minimum, and that refusal is the whole point of the guard. |
| `gpu.guard` | ERROR / INFO | This is the verdict a launch would get at this moment, with the reasons the guard would give for it. |
| `gpu.driver-resets` | WARN | A display driver reset under load takes the Editor and the model down together, and a machine that has had one recently will have another. |
| `gpu.lock` | WARN / INFO | One process at a time may load the model, and a command that appears to hang is often waiting for whoever holds the lock. |

### `vram.headroom` — Video memory headroom for the preset

- Reports: ERROR / WARN
- Fix: Free video memory, choose a preset with a smaller context, or set guard.allowOffload so the part that does not fit runs from system RAM.
- Source: spec 7.3 and 7.4

### `gpu.guard` — Guard verdict right now

- Reports: ERROR / INFO
- Fix: Close what is using the GPU, or read the listed reasons and decide which one to act on.
- Source: spec 7.3

### `gpu.driver-resets` — Recent display driver resets

- Reports: WARN
- Fix: Lower the context size or the guard thresholds, and check the vendor driver release notes.
- Source: spec 5.4

### `gpu.lock` — GPU lock holder

- Reports: WARN / INFO
- Fix: Wait for the holder to finish, or delete the lock file once you are sure the process is gone.
- Source: spec 7.8

## Permissions

| Check | Reports | What it detects, and why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `permissions.serialized-assets` | ERROR | A scene, prefab, asset or meta file rewritten by a model loses references that no diff review catches, and the damage shows up days later in the Editor. |
| `permissions.vcs-writes` | ERROR | A commit, push, submit or checkin the model decided to run is the one action a reviewer cannot undo by rejecting a diff. |
| `permissions.auto-approve-risk` | WARN | A blanket allow turns every later ask into silence, which is exactly the setting that makes an agent look well behaved right up to the moment it is not. |

### `permissions.serialized-assets` — Serialized Unity assets denied

- Reports: ERROR
- Fix: Deny edit and read for the serialized-asset globs, and let the model change C# only.
- Source: spec 8.5.4

### `permissions.vcs-writes` — Version-control writes denied

- Reports: ERROR
- Fix: Deny the version-control write commands for the agent's bash tool.
- Source: spec 8.5.3 and 8.5.4

### `permissions.auto-approve-risk` — Dangerous actions still ask

- Reports: WARN
- Fix: Replace the blanket allow with the narrow patterns the action actually needs.
- Source: spec 8.5

## Unity project

| Check | Reports | What it detects, and why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `unity.compile-check` | WARN | Without a generated project file and a .NET SDK the agent cannot compile what it wrote, so a change is reviewed on the strength of how plausible it reads. |

### `unity.compile-check` — Compile check available

- Reports: WARN
- Fix: Open the project in Unity once to generate the project files, and install a .NET SDK.
- Source: spec 9.3

### `unity.facts-stale` — Project facts current

- Reports: WARN
- Fix: Run opencode-unity init --refresh.
- Source: spec 9.8

### `unity.opencode-dir` — No .opencode folder in the project

- Reports: WARN
- Fix: Remove the folder, or add it to the ignore file for this version control system.
- Source: OpenCode config/config.ts and spec 9.4

### `unity.project-found` — Unity project found

- Reports: WARN / INFO
- Fix: Point doctor at a Unity project directory, or pass --project <dir>.
- Source: spec 5.4
